note: Curriculum-review artifact, not finished lesson prose. Sequenced pedagogically, not alphabetically. Every learning point traces to at least one evidence-requirement claim in EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json.
revisionNote: This is a corrected revision following Product Architect review, which held the original 16 VERIFIED / 17-learning-point claim pending a depth-and-granularity correction pass (see PROJECT-STATUS.md and EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json's paDepthCorrectionNote for the full disposition). Eight learning points were added (decimal four operations; percentage of another quantity; direct proportion/unit-value method; algebraic notation/variables; substitution and order of operations; and mean, median, mode, and range split out of one combined point), none were removed, and several were corrected in wording, depth, or application example. Learning-point IDs were renumbered throughout to reflect the corrected instructional sequence.

learningPoints.title: Equivalent fractions and simplifying
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to recognise when two fractions are equivalent and simplify a fraction to its lowest terms.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A fraction can be rewritten in an equivalent form (e.g. 1/2 = 2/4 = 50/100); a fraction is simplified to lowest terms by cancelling a common factor from numerator and denominator.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Matches AC1.1 identify/apply at Level 2; equivalence and simplifying only, no formal proof of fraction equality.
applicationTypes: Simplify a given fraction to its lowest terms, e.g. 6/8.

learningPoints.title: The four operations on fractions
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to add, subtract, multiply, and divide fractions.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Adding/subtracting fractions requires a common denominator; multiplying fractions multiplies numerators and denominators directly; dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Straightforward Level 2 vocational numeric application; matches AC1.1 apply.
applicationTypes: Add two component tolerance fractions, e.g. 1/4 + 1/6.
Divide a total quantity of cable by a fractional length per run.

learningPoints.title: Decimal place value and multiplying/dividing by powers of ten
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to state the place value of a digit in a decimal number and multiply or divide a decimal by 10, 100, 1000 (and their negative-power equivalents) by shifting the decimal point.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Each column in a decimal number is ten times its right-hand neighbour; multiplying by a power of ten shifts digits left, dividing shifts them right (e.g. 0.507 x 100 = 50.7; 127.5 / 10 = 12.75).
learningPoints.depthJustification: Directly needed for unit-prefix conversions (mA, kΩ) in later electrical calculations; matches AC1.1.
explicitExclusions: Manual long-column addition/subtraction algorithms (assumed prior knowledge)
applicationTypes: Convert 0.075 A to mA by shifting the decimal point three places.

learningPoints.title: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing decimals
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to calculate with decimal quantities using addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Decimals are added or subtracted by lining up their decimal points (using placeholder zeros as needed) and calculating as whole numbers; decimals are multiplied by multiplying as whole numbers and then placing the decimal point so the product has as many decimal places as the two factors combined; one decimal is divided by another by moving both numbers' decimal points the same number of places to make the divisor a whole number, then dividing.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: the original inventory covered decimal place value and powers of ten but not calculation with decimals, which a requirement named 'ordinary decimal arithmetic' requires at the approved depth. Calculator-supported computation is acceptable and expected in practice; the procedure is taught here for conceptual understanding of decimal-point placement (why the answer has the shape it does), not to mandate manual column-algorithm mastery as an assessed skill in its own right.
explicitExclusions: Manual long-column arithmetic as an assessed skill in itself (calculator-supported calculation is acceptable)
Recurring/non-terminating decimal arithmetic beyond recognising the dot notation (covered in FM-LP-05)
applicationTypes: Add the measured lengths of several cable offcuts given to two decimal places.
Multiply a unit cost given in decimal pounds by a decimal quantity to find a total.

learningPoints.title: Converting between fractions, decimals and percentages
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to convert a value between fraction, decimal, and percentage form.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A fraction converts to a decimal by dividing numerator by denominator; a decimal converts to a fraction using its place value; a percentage is a fraction with denominator 100, so percentage-decimal-fraction conversions follow by multiplying/dividing by 100 or re-expressing over 100.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Core Level 2 numeracy skill; recurring non-terminating decimals (e.g. 1/3) noted but not explored theoretically.
explicitExclusions: Continued/repeating decimal notation beyond recognising the dot notation
applicationTypes: Express a measured proportion (e.g. 3/8 of a circuit's rated current) as a decimal and a percentage.

learningPoints.title: Finding a percentage of a quantity
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to explain what a percentage represents and calculate a given percentage of a quantity.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A percentage is a fraction with denominator 100 (symbol %); to find x% of a quantity, convert x% to the fraction x/100 and multiply by the quantity.
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-PERCENTAGES: finding a percentage of a quantity portion
learningPoints.depthJustification: Matches AC1.1 identify/apply; excludes compound/repeated-percentage theory per the approved depth decision precedent set for this topic in pilot-002.
explicitExclusions: Reverse percentages (finding an original amount before a percentage change)
applicationTypes: Calculate 15% of a batch of 240 components produced in a shift.

learningPoints.title: Expressing one quantity as a percentage of another
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to express one quantity as a percentage of another quantity of the same kind.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: To express one quantity as a percentage of another, write the first quantity as a fraction of the second, then divide the numerator by the denominator and multiply by 100% (e.g. 18 out of 20 is 18/20 = 90%).
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-PERCENT-OF-ANOTHER: express one quantity as a percentage of another
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: needed for calculations such as efficiency (a comparison of two quantities), which finding-a-percentage-of-a-quantity alone does not provide. Kept as a separate learning point from FM-LP-06 so the two distinct skills -- finding a percentage OF a quantity, and expressing one quantity AS a percentage of another -- can be diagnosed independently.
applicationTypes: Express 18 correct answers out of 20 test questions as a percentage.

learningPoints.title: Ratio notation and simplifying ratios
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to express a comparison between two or more quantities as a ratio and simplify it to its lowest-term form.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A ratio compares similar quantities using colon notation (e.g. 2:5); ratios must use the same units before simplifying; a ratio is simplified by cancelling a common factor, in the same way as a fraction.
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-RATIOS: ratio notation and simplifying portion
learningPoints.depthJustification: Foundational for ratio and proportion work later in Unit 202 (not itself evidence that any specific electrical relationship expressed as a ratio has been acquired).
explicitExclusions: Ratios involving three or more unlike-unit quantities without conversion
applicationTypes: Simplify a paint-mixing ratio, e.g. 250 ml to 50 ml.

learningPoints.title: Sharing a quantity in a given ratio
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to divide a quantity into parts according to a given ratio.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: To share a quantity in a given ratio: add the ratio's parts to find the total number of parts, divide the quantity by that total to find the value of one part, then multiply by each ratio number to find each share.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Direct proportion only, matching this requirement's PROCEDURE/CALCULATION_METHOD dimensions; no inverse-proportion theory.
applicationTypes: Share a 12 m length of cable between three work packages in the ratio 3:2:1.

learningPoints.title: Direct proportion: scaling and the unit-value method
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to scale a quantity in direct proportion, including finding a unit value and scaling from it, and applying a known ratio or proportional relationship to find an unknown quantity.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A quantity is scaled in direct proportion by first finding the amount corresponding to a single unit (dividing the known amount by the number of units it represents), then multiplying that unit amount by however many units are required. This is the same unit-value technique used to find the value of one part when sharing a quantity in a given ratio (FM-LP-09), applied instead to scale a quantity up or down.
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-RATIOS: direct-proportion scaling / unit-value method portion
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: ratio notation, simplifying, and sharing in a ratio do not by themselves cover the direct-proportion reasoning needed to execute Unit 202 calculations that scale a known relationship (e.g. scaling a quantity given a known rate). Inverse proportion is deliberately excluded -- no requirement in this repository's 213-item Unit 202 evidence-requirement plan currently names it, so it is not taught speculatively; this exclusion should be revisited if a later production batch (e.g. mechanics-and-machines, which includes a separate gear-ratio/speed relationship requirement) surfaces a genuine need for it. No electrical application example is used here for an electrical relationship that has not yet been acquired.
explicitExclusions: Inverse proportion (explicitly excluded pending evidence of a genuine Unit 202 need -- none found in the current 213-requirement plan)
applicationTypes: Find the cost of 8 identical fixings given the cost of 5 of the same fixing, using the unit-value method.

learningPoints.title: Algebraic notation: variables and reading conventional notation
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to explain what a variable is and read conventional algebraic notation, including implicit multiplication and superscript (power) notation.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A variable is a letter used to stand for a quantity that can take different values (e.g. v for speed); by convention, a number multiplying a variable is written without a multiplication symbol (5 x a is written 5a); a superscript denotes a power (4^2 means 4 x 4).
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-MATHLANGUAGE: variable definition and notation conventions
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: the algebra requirement's original single-source evidence (brackets/like terms) did not cover the meaning of a variable or the conventions for reading algebraic notation, both needed before formula use and transposition. 'Constant' and 'coefficient' are not independently defined by name in the cited source (it demonstrates the underlying idea operationally, e.g. 5a, without using that vocabulary) -- this is recorded honestly rather than overclaimed; the functional skill of reading and using such notation is still evidenced.
explicitExclusions: Formal named vocabulary for 'constant' and 'coefficient' (not sourced to a permitted-authority document this pass; the underlying ideas are taught operationally)
applicationTypes: Read and interpret an expression such as 5a + 3 appearing on a technical worksheet.

learningPoints.title: Expanding a single bracket and collecting like terms
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to expand an algebraic expression containing a single bracket and simplify the result by collecting like terms.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: The term outside a bracket multiplies each term inside it (e.g. a(b+c) = ab+ac; 3(x+2) = 3x+6); after expanding, terms of the same kind are collected together to simplify the expression.
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-ALGEBRA-BRACKETS: expanding brackets and collecting like terms
learningPoints.depthJustification: Foundational notation needed before formula transposition; no equation-solving or factorising introduced here.
explicitExclusions: Expanding a product of two brackets
applicationTypes: Simplify an expression combining two component values, e.g. 5 + 2(x+1).

learningPoints.title: Substituting into a formula and evaluating using the correct order of operations
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to substitute given numerical values into an expression or formula and evaluate the result using the correct order of operations.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Numerical values are substituted into a formula in place of its variables and then evaluated using the correct order of operations (BODMAS: Brackets, pOwers, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction), e.g. for v = u + at with u=5, a=2, t=3: v = 5 + 2 x 3 = 11, where the multiplication is carried out before the addition.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: substitution into a formula and evaluating the result correctly is the algebra skill most directly used throughout Unit 202's calculation work, and was entirely absent from the original single-source evidence. This is a distinct, independently diagnosable skill from expanding brackets, so it is kept as its own learning point rather than folded into FM-LP-12.
explicitExclusions: Solving for an unknown that is not already isolated (that is formula transposition, FM-LP-16/FM-LP-17)
applicationTypes: Substitute given values into the formula s = ut + (1/2)at^2 and evaluate the result in the correct order.

learningPoints.title: Laws of indices for positive whole-number powers
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to state what an index (power) means and apply the laws of indices to simplify expressions involving positive powers.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: An index shows repeated multiplication of a quantity by itself; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn); a^m / a^n = a^(m-n); a^0 = 1.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Whole-number positive powers only; matches AC1.1. Essential prerequisite for engineering notation and squared-formula transposition.
applicationTypes: Simplify a repeated-multiplication expression such as a^2 x a^3.

learningPoints.title: Negative indices
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to interpret and evaluate a negative index as a reciprocal power.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A negative index means 'one over' the corresponding positive power: a^(-1) = 1/a; a^(-m) = 1/(a^m).
learningPoints.depthJustification: Essential for standard form (negative exponents) and unit prefixes below the base unit (e.g. milli-, micro-).
applicationTypes: Interpret 10^-3 as 1/1000 when converting a unit prefix.

learningPoints.title: Rearranging a simple formula to make a different variable the subject
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to rearrange a simple linear formula to make a stated variable the subject, using one or more inverse operations.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A formula stays balanced if the same operation is performed on both sides; to isolate a variable, perform the inverse operation of whatever separates it from the rest of the formula, one operation at a time (e.g. v = u + at rearranged for t: subtract u from both sides, then divide by a, giving t = (v-u)/a -- two inverse operations, not one).
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: the worked example v = u + at rearranged for t requires two inverse operations (subtract, then divide), not one -- this learning point and its underlying claim are corrected from an earlier, inaccurate 'single-step'/'single balanced operation' description. Directly reused as the foundational procedure for Ohm's law and other Unit 202 formula rearrangements once those relationships are themselves acquired in a later production batch.
explicitExclusions: Formulae involving powers or roots (see FM-LP-17)
applicationTypes: Rearrange the formula v = u + at (as taught in this procedure's own source material) to make t the subject.

learningPoints.title: Rearranging formulae involving squares and square roots
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to rearrange a formula containing a squared term or a square root to make a stated variable the subject.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Squaring both sides removes a square root; taking the square root of both sides undoes a square (e.g. v^2 = u^2 + 2as rearranged for u: u = sqrt(v^2 - 2as)); the pendulum formula T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g) rearranged for g by squaring, multiplying, and dividing.
learningPoints.depthJustification: A commonly predictable misconception is forgetting to take the square root as the final step; this is directly needed for formulae such as impedance calculations later in Unit 202 once that relationship is itself acquired.
applicationTypes: Rearrange a squared-term formula to find an unknown base value.

learningPoints.title: Standard (scientific) form
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to write a number as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten, following the pattern of a single non-zero digit before the decimal point, and interpret a number already given in that form.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: A number can be written as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten (e.g. 9.52 x 10^-3); the sign and size of the exponent indicate how many places the decimal point moves. The evidenced examples of this format all use a coefficient with a single non-zero digit before the decimal point.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Needed to read instrument displays and datasheet values. PA depth correction: the underlying evidence-requirement status is PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, not VERIFIED -- a capped search across this requirement's permitted authority classes (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY, PROFESSIONAL_BODY, AUTHORITATIVE_TECHNICAL_REFERENCE) did not find a source stating the precise universal convention that the coefficient's magnitude must satisfy 1 <= |a| < 10; see EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json's gaps entry for this requirement. This learning point is scoped to teach only the coefficient-times-power-of-ten pattern as actually demonstrated by the cited source's own examples (each of which happens to use a single leading non-zero digit), rather than asserting an unsourced universal rule. This scoping gap should be closed with a further targeted source before this point is treated as fully evidenced.
explicitExclusions: A formally sourced statement of the universal 1 <= |a| < 10 bound (flagged as an open sourcing gap, not asserted)
applicationTypes: Write a measured resistance of 4,700,000 ohms in standard form.

learningPoints.title: Engineering notation and SI unit prefixes
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to write a number in engineering notation and relate it to the correct SI unit prefix.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: Engineering notation restricts the power-of-ten exponent to multiples of 3, so it lines up with SI prefixes (e.g. 33 x 10^6 Hz = 33 MHz); the coefficient is conventionally kept between about 0.1 and 1000.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Directly needed to read and write electrical quantities using k, M, m, µ prefixes throughout Unit 202. Unlike standard form (FM-LP-18), this requirement's convention (multiples-of-3 exponents, coefficient 0.1-1000) is stated explicitly and completely by the cited NIST source, so it remains fully VERIFIED.
explicitExclusions: Uncommon/legacy prefixes outside the standard SI set
applicationTypes: Express 0.000068 A in engineering notation and as an SI-prefixed unit (68 µA).

learningPoints.title: Pythagoras' theorem
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to state Pythagoras' theorem, use it to find the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle, and rearrange it to find a shorter side.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c^2 = a^2 + b^2. The theorem is used directly to find the hypotenuse (c = sqrt(a^2+b^2)), and, by rearranging, to find either shorter side when the hypotenuse and the other shorter side are known (e.g. b = sqrt(c^2-a^2)).
normalizedClaimRefs: SRC-PYTHAGORAS: theorem statement and worked procedure for finding an unknown side
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: the original evidence quoted only the theorem statement, while this learning point's outcome already promised finding an unknown side -- an unsupported procedural promise. The same, already-cited source's second page (previously under-quoted) contains worked examples for both finding the hypotenuse and finding a shorter side, closing the gap. Needed for right-angled-triangle-style calculations later in the qualification once the relevant electrical relationship is itself acquired.
applicationTypes: Find the length of the diagonal brace needed for a rectangular frame of known width and height.

learningPoints.title: Sine, cosine and tangent ratios in right-angled triangles (SOHCAHTOA)
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to state the sine, cosine, and tangent ratios for a right-angled triangle and use the appropriate ratio to find an unknown side given one side and one non-right angle.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse; cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan A = opposite/adjacent (SOHCAHTOA); given one side and a non-right angle, the matching ratio is rearranged to find the unknown side.
learningPoints.depthJustification: Right-angled-triangle ratios for finding an unknown SIDE only, matching this requirement's depth ceiling; excludes the sine/cosine rule for general triangles. PA depth correction: the full 213-requirement Unit 202 evidence-requirement plan was reviewed for any requirement naming phase angle, power factor, or an unknown-angle calculation; none was found, so finding an unknown ANGLE using inverse trigonometric functions is explicitly excluded from this batch rather than added speculatively. This exclusion should be revisited if the electromagnetism/AC-theory production batch surfaces a genuine need for it.
explicitExclusions: Sine rule and cosine rule (non-right-angled triangles)
Finding an unknown angle using inverse trigonometric functions (explicitly excluded pending evidence of a genuine Unit 202 need -- none found in the current 213-requirement plan)
applicationTypes: Find the height gained by a ramp of known length inclined at a known angle.

learningPoints.title: Arithmetic mean
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to calculate the arithmetic mean of a small, ungrouped data set.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: The mean of a data set is the sum of the data points divided by the number of data points.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: split out of a single combined mean/median/mode/range learning point so the adaptive model can independently diagnose which specific calculation or concept a learner has misunderstood. May still be taught together with FM-LP-23/24/25 in one lesson; the assessment/diagnostic granularity is what requires separation. Ungrouped small data sets only.
applicationTypes: Calculate the mean of a set of repeated test-instrument readings.

learningPoints.title: Median
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to find the median of a small, ungrouped data set.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: The median of a data set is the middle value when the data are arranged in order (half the data are smaller, half larger); for an even number of data points, the median is the mean of the two middle values.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: split out of a single combined mean/median/mode/range learning point for independent diagnosability. Ungrouped small data sets only.
applicationTypes: Find the median of a set of repeated test-instrument readings.

learningPoints.title: Mode
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to find the mode of a small, ungrouped data set.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: The mode of a data set is the value that occurs with the greatest frequency.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: split out of a single combined mean/median/mode/range learning point for independent diagnosability. Ungrouped small data sets only.
applicationTypes: Find the mode of a set of repeated test-instrument readings.

learningPoints.title: Range
learningPoints.learnerOutcome: The learner will be able to calculate the range of a small, ungrouped data set.
learningPoints.knowledgeOrProcedure: The range of a data set is the largest value minus the smallest value.
learningPoints.depthJustification: PA depth correction: split out of a single combined mean/median/mode/range learning point for independent diagnosability. Ungrouped small data sets only.
applicationTypes: Calculate the range of a set of repeated test-instrument readings.

partiallyEvidencedLearningPoints.note: Not held -- the core skill (writing/interpreting a number as coefficient x power of ten, single leading non-zero digit) is evidenced by example and remains READY. The underlying evidence requirement (standard-scientific-notation) is PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, not VERIFIED, because a precise universal statement of the coefficient bound (1 <= |a| < 10) was not found in a permitted-authority source this pass. See EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json's gaps entry for this requirement.
